claims.claim_text: The indexed Harold G Nelson is a high-confidence match to the reviewed official records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed name, Technician Third Grade rank, and nonshared protected identifier agree with a 9 May 1945 OSS Operational Group special order.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. Exact name, rank, and a nonshared protected identifier agree in two official records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The order documents an OSS Special Reconnaissance Battalion assignment on 9 May 1945 but does not identify the immediately preceding assignment or a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The operational assignment is identity context only; it is not converted into a pre-OSS employer or immediate predecessor claim.

claims.temporal_assessment: The bulk row's coded entry date is after the war and cannot establish pre-OSS chronology; no named employer is supplied.
claims.match_notes: The anomalous coded date is preserved as a reason not to infer chronology; no coded occupation is converted into employer evidence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Ingolv Nelson is a high-confidence match to the reviewed official records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Exact name and a nonshared protected identifier agree with the official Army bulk record; an Army Special Operations history independently names Sgt Ingolv Nelson on the OSS Maritime Unit P-101 crew.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. The official identifier match and uncommon-name OSS crew record independently align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish Army and OSS Maritime Unit context but do not identify the immediately preceding assignment or a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: No coded Army occupation is converted into employer evidence, and the 1945 crew record is not labeled as pre-OSS.
